title: KV compactor: staged fidelity gating + memory-aware batching for INT4/INT8/FP8 trials
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Design and run controlled experiments for a staged KV compaction ("compactors") pipeline that performs per-shard fidelity gating and memory-aware continuous batching to enable aggressive quantization (INT4/INT8/FP8) without unacceptable degradation in end-to-end model quality. The goal is a pragmatic fallback/rollout strategy that saves GPU memory under tail-loads and cold-start pressure while preserving production SLOs for latency and top-line quality metrics.

Motivation: Current KV cache footprints are a dominant driver of peak GPU memory. Prior work explored raw quant schemes and blockwise packing but left two practical gaps: 1) safe, per-cohort fidelity decisions when traffic mixes cohorts with different sensitivity; 2) interactions between continuous batching windows and quantized KV read/write patterns that can amplify reconstruction errors under high concurrency. This ticket scopes a reproducible experiment plan, monitoring hooks, and a rolloutable runtime prototype that exercises INT4/INT8/FP8 compaction with gating rules based on cohort error budgets and latency headroom.

Outcomes expected: measured memory reduction, per-token quality delta across cohorts, end-to-end latency impact under realistic batching, and a recommended fidelity controller with conservative defaults for canary and gradual ramping.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype runtime that can compress KV shards to FP8/INT8/INT4 at write-time and decompress at read-time with <1.5ms additional median token latency on p4d-like hardware
Memory reduction: >=25% median KV footprint and >=40% tail (95th) improvement for long-context sessions vs baseline uncompressed cache
Quality guardrails: no cohort should regress more than 1.2% on the designated rerank/QA eval suite; worst-case token-level perplexity increase <2% for evaluated instruction-following dataset

Fidelity gating controller exposes per-shard policy and an emergency discard path; includes metrics that trigger automatic synchronous fallback to uncompressed shards when quality or latency thresholds exceeded

Observability: dashboards for compressed/uncompressed hit rates, reconstruction error distribution, per-cohort quality, and end-to-end SLOs; synthetic replay harness and traffic slice report available in Confluence
experiment_plan: Phase 0 - Labbed sims (3 days): offline simulation on replayed traces (sampled user cohorts + open instruction datasets). Implement fast quantizers for FP8/INT8/INT4, evaluate reconstruction error distributions, and generate fidelity maps per-token and per-layer.

Phase 1 - Controlled canary (5 days): runtime prototype in a canary pool (10% of dedicated nodes). Enable per-shard compaction at write time with read-time transparent decompression. Measure memory, tail latency, and cohort-specific quality. Canary configured with conservative gating (only INT8 for hot shards, FP8 as intermediate).

Phase 2 - Mixed fidelity experiments (7 days): enable mixed policies: (A) aggressive INT4 for cold shards + per-cohort fallback; (B) INT8 for medium-tone shards; (C) FP8 as a balanced default. Run A/B comparisons across traffic slices (interactive chat vs. long-batch generation).

Phase 3 - Continuous batching stress (4 days): replay high-concurrency traces with continuous batching windows enabled. Observe interactions: KV read amplification, cache reconstruction rate, and batching latency. Tune batch window limits and cache prefetch heuristics.

Phase 4 - Rollout readiness & docs (3 days): finalize controller defaults, define monitoring alerts, document rollback steps, and prepare release notes and API flags for Dedicated/Private deployments.
metrics: Memory: median and 95th percentile KV bytes per GPU, per-session memory delta vs baseline
Quality: cohort-level rerank accuracy, instruction-following QA F1, and token-level perplexity; percent of sessions exceeding quality budget
Latency: median token generation latency, 95th/99th percentiles, and additional serialization/deserialization overhead introduced by compaction
Throughput: effective tokens/sec per GPU under continuous batching with compaction enabled
Operational: compaction success rate, decompression error rate, on-path fallback rate, and gate-trigger frequency
rollout_plan: Start: internal skeleton on dedicated canary pool with traffic shadowing for 48 hours. No user-facing rollout until sanity metrics stable.
Canary: enable read/write compaction for 5% of traffic with automatic circuit-breaker that disables compaction if latency or quality thresholds trip for 1 minute continuously.
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 3-4 days with manual verification at each step. Keep conservative default policies (INT8 preferred for hot shards).

Fallback: immediate per-shard fallback to uncompressed cache if quality delta > threshold OR decompression errors observed. Rollback path documented in runbook with commands for disabling compaction on a pool.

Final: merge config flags and controller into runtime and ship as behind-a-feature-flag release for Dedicated and Private; recommend Managed (hosted) gradual rollout after 2 weeks of Dedicated stability.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: INT4 reconstruction error interacts badly with attention KV updates causing hallucination regressions. Mitigation: conservative cohort gating; block-level checksums and reconstruction error monitors that trigger synchronous fallback.

Risk: Decompression CPU overhead pushes token latency over SLO during bursts. Mitigation: offload decompression to async worker threads, measure CPU/SM tradeoffs and add fast-path for cache hits where decompression skipped for hot keys.
Risk: Interactive workloads sensitive to minute quality deltas. Mitigation: keep hot interactive shards at higher fidelity (FP8/INT8) and reserve INT4 for long-context archival shards only.

Risk: Undetected data corruption on write-time compaction. Mitigation: add write-time validation checksums and a periodic integrity scrub that can reconstruct from uncompressed shadow storage if necessary.

2026-03-06 SRE review (Jordan Lee): Flagged decompression CPU as potential bottleneck on smaller instance types. Action: add CPU profiling to Phase 1 and gate canary on CPU headroom.

2026-03-10 PM review (Rina Kaur): Requested clearer rollout thresholds and customer impact classification. Marked customer_impact as 'medium' for now. Added acceptance criteria for quality budgets.
